name: upgrade_pydantic_min_anystr_length_to_str_min_length
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: min_anystr_length=3 to 2.x ConfigDict(str_min_length=3) - the v1 key is silently ignored under pydantic 2.x, so the minimum-length constraint is never enforced on any string field; incomplete-fix broken switches to the ConfigDict container but keeps the stale v1 key name, so nothing actually changes
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Tag in tag.py uses the pydantic 1.x `class Config: min_anystr_length = 3` pattern to reject any string field shorter than 3 characters, project-wide. Under the installed pydantic 2.x, this key is silently ignored (unrecognized), so a name like "ab" is now wrongly accepted. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: `model_config = ConfigDict(str_min_length=3)` as a class attribute. A name shorter than 3 characters must be rejected after the fix; "abc" (exactly 3) must still be accepted.

test_setup_files.test_tag.py:
from tag import Tag

t = Tag(name="abc")
assert t.name == "abc"

try:
    Tag(name="ab")
    raise AssertionError("expected a name shorter than 3 characters to be rejected")
except AssertionError:
    raise
except Exception:
    pass

print("PASS")

reference_solution.tag.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Tag(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_min_length=3)

    name: str

files.tag.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Tag(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(min_anystr_length=3)

    name: str
